title: Amazon Buys Decart's AI Chip Tech for $7.5B to Take On Nvidia
yt_title: Amazon Buys Decart's AI Chip Tech for $7.5B to Take On Nvidia
yt_description:
Amazon is buying the Decart Optimization Stack, the AI chip optimization tech from Israeli startup Decart, and hiring its founders, in a deal Bloomberg valued at about $7.5 billion. The goal: make Amazon's own Trainium chips faster and cheaper as it prepares to sell them to outside customers and take on Nvidia. Plus the twist: Anthropic was in talks to buy Decart for around $6 billion before walking away.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Amazon just went shopping, and the bill is seven and a half billion dollars! The target? Decart, a three-year-old AI startup from Israel, best known for real-time video and interactive world models. But Amazon is not buying the whole company. It is buying Decart's secret sauce: a tool called the Decart Optimization Stack. That software squeezes more speed out of AI chips, so models run faster and cheaper on the same hardware. And Amazon is hiring the founders too: brothers Dean and Orian Leitersdorf, plus their team of researchers and engineers. Bloomberg put the price at about seven and a half billion dollars. Amazon itself did not disclose the terms. Reports say the money comes in cash and stock, in installments tied to targets over five years. No pressure! Why so much? Two words: Trainium chips. Amazon's own AI chips, built by its Annapurna Labs team. Amazon has used Trainium inside its own data centers. Now it is preparing to sell them to outside customers. Andy Jassy says he expects a very significant business selling chips externally. Hello, Nvidia! Decart already knows these chips. Amazon said Decart ran real-time video four times faster on Trainium, at half the cost of GPUs. Amazon's Peter DeSantis says every leap in AI starts with getting more out of every chip. And here is the twist: earlier this year, Anthropic was in talks to buy Decart for around six billion dollars. Anthropic walked away in September. Nvidia, a Decart investor, also passed. Then Amazon swooped in! The deal still needs regulators to sign off. But the message is loud: the AI chip war is now a software war too! Want the full story?
